questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was told that the University Of Barcelona was a good University, and it was also a good opportunity to explore the spanish culture along with the Catalan culture in an aspect of cultural differences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find information. In the beginning it was a little hard to understand how it all worked at the University, because it's different from Copenhagen both in the way of teaching which I find to be a little more practical in Barcelona and also the differences in exams.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introduction one of the first days where information was provided, and we also had a person we could tall to when we needed information on a specific subject. This came in very handy from time to time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was easy for me because I knew the places to find it. And I had some connections but when I was using
idealista.es
it seemed a little frustrating because you can't go see the place because of the long distance. So You really have to rely on honest people when finding a flat.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That is it a good opportunity to live with locals.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was easy. In the introduction days we had the opportunity to change the courses if we didn't like the ones we had chosen. This was possible within the first 3 weeks. Registration office helped us find the right courses and schedule to make it all fit together. From there you had your personal ID number and access to the virtual campus where most of the material and stuff could be found from the classes. Also we were given a student card.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a person who worked with all of the erramos students who was available both by e-mail and during office hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the clases I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be present in the intro days because this is where a lot of information is given.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was very mixed in my experience. All of the clases had 6 ECTS each. But some clases were very heavy compared to others. Both in the material that you had to read and also the final exam. Overall the level was very aline with the level from the home university, but since everything is in a foreign language this can be a little overwhelming, especially in the beginning of the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I find the teaching to be a little more practical at UB because there are different ways to pass. Doing all the practical stuff during the semester gives you points that gives you the opportunity to pass the exam without having to attend one single exam at the end of the semester. I also find that the teaching in some ways at least in my classes was with a hint of philosophy. Overall the teaching was very effective and gave me the tools I needed for the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Spanish sociolinguistics. 
Introduction to linguistics. 
Culture and Communication.
Semiotics of Communication. 
Text production in Spanish.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them were interesting in their own way but I find Culture and Communication to be the most interesting because of all the different aspects the course had to it which was culture, communication, globalization, journalism. Also Semiotics of Communication was exiting because it was a new way of leaning about communication especially within the media field.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In my flat because of the inflation gas, electricity, water was a little unexpected. Because these bills were high which was around 750 DKK extra each month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was not a little more expensive then I expected, but this was because of the inflation. Transportation was also a little expensive. Housing is more or less the same, but going for a coffee was cheap. Around 10 DKK for a cup of coffee in a café.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of cultural activities outside of school, both in meeting and the eramus students who arranged a lot of activities around the city. This was clubbing, sightseeing and other activities to explore both the culture and meet new people. The whole experience was very vibrant.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus activities gives you a lot of social connections which is very nice outside of school. Usually there is made a group in WhatsApp in the intro days where activities are published.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city. The city is so big and has a lot to offer. In the summer the weather gives you the opportunity to live the beach life and travel to other parts of Catalonia or Spain.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy the Catalan/spanish people are very friendly and even though your Spanish is not perfect they really try to help you express yourself. This way it was very easy to talk to people because you feel very welcomed by the locals.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In my classes the majority were locals. Start a conversation and be a part of the group work in class this opens the door and shows that you are interested in meeting them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One thing that was a little hard was that the local students in my classes sometimes spoke in Catalan. Also sometimes with the teacher even though I chose the classes in Spanish. So sometimes I missed some questions because of this, you are allowed to ask if they can translate into spanish but since a lot of students do it, it feels weird to ask all the time. But mostly the questions were answered by the teacher in Spanish.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked the diversity in the culture and the food. It was a magical experience to explore spanish and Catalan culture in a mix. Because Barcelona is a big city you have everything. If you go outside of the city you will find towns where the Catalan culture and language are very dominant. This was exiting to see.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Make sure your housing is comfortable for you 
2: Attend the intro days and classes.
3: Socialize with the locals and the other Erasmus students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you really understand how the exams work from the beginning. Because in Barcelona and Spain in general the exams are very different from Denmark, the point system and grades are different as well. Take your time to understand what is important for you to pass the exams, because the point system starts within the first couple of week if you attend the practical work in class and it will have an influence on your final grade.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole experience of going abroad. The culture, the people and especially the language. When you are in a country where the language you are studying is spoken it gives you the opportunity to really utilize it and make it better. So for me the most rewarding thing was the evolvement of my spoken language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was to understand how the whole system of the university and how it worked. This is why it's super important to attend the intro days and ask questions if you have any. Don't be shy to ask because you will benefit from it in the end. It's not fun to reach the end of the semester and find out that there are things you are unsure of.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
